{{Short description|Canadian mathematician (1943–1987)}}
{{About|the Canadian mathematician Evelyn Nelson|the American silent film actress|Evelyn Nelson}}

'''Evelyn Merle Nelson''' (November 25, 1943 &ndash; August 1, 1987),<ref name="macTutor">{{MacTutor|id=Nelson|title=Evelyn Nelson|date=April 2002}}</ref> born '''Evelyn Merle Roden''', was a [[Canadians|Canadian]] [[mathematician]]. Nelson made contributions to the area of [[universal algebra]] with applications to [[theoretical computer science]]. She, along with [[Cecilia Krieger]], is the namesake of the [[Krieger–Nelson Prize]],
awarded by the [[Canadian Mathematical Society]] for outstanding research by a female mathematician.<ref name="cmsBio">[http://www.cms.math.ca/Prizes/info/kn.html Krieger-Nelson Prize], [[Canadian Mathematical Society]].</ref>

==Early life==
Nelson was born on November 25, 1943, in [[Hamilton, Ontario]], Canada. Her parents were immigrants from [[Russia]] in the 1920s.<ref name="banaschewski">{{citation|doi=10.1007/BF01211834|first=B.|last=Banaschewski|title=Evelyn M. Nelson: An Appreciation|journal=[[Algebra Universalis]]|volume=26|issue=3|year=1989|pages=259–266|s2cid=120567997}}.</ref> Nelson went to high school at [[Westdale Secondary School]] in Hamilton.<ref name="banaschewski" />

==Education==
After spending two years at the [[University of Toronto]], Nelson returned to [[Hamilton, Ontario|Hamilton]] to study at [[McMaster University]]. She received her [[Bachelor of Science|B.Sc]] in [[mathematics]] from
McMaster in 1965, followed by an [[Master's degree|M.Sc.]] in mathematics from McMaster in 1967. She succeeded in having her thesis work published in the ''[[Canadian Journal of Mathematics]]'', also in 1967; the article was entitled "Finiteness of semigroups of operators in universal algebra".<ref name="macTutor" />

Nelson completed her [[Ph.D.]] in 1970. Her thesis was entitled "The lattice of equational classes of commutative semigroups", and the ideas also formed a journal paper published in the [[Canadian Journal of Mathematics]].<ref name="banaschewski" /><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=38541|name=Evelyn M. Nelson}}</ref>

==Career==
Following completion of her Ph.D., Nelson continued at McMaster. She first worked as a post-doctoral researcher, later as a "research associate", and in 1978 was appointed [[associate professor]].<ref name="banaschewski" /> Serving as chair of the Unit of Computer Science at McMaster from 1982 until 1984, Nelson became a full [[professor]] in 1983.<ref name="order">{{citation|doi=10.1007/BF00354888|title=Obituary: Evelyn M. Nelson|journal=[[Order (journal)|Order]]|volume=5|year=1988|issue=3|pages=221–223|s2cid=189901469}}.</ref>

Nelson's teaching record was, according to one colleague, "invariably of the highest order". However, before earning a faculty position at McMaster, prejudice against her led to doubts about her teaching ability.<ref name="banaschewski" />

Nelson published over 40 papers during her 20-year career. She died from [[cancer]] in 1987.<ref name="banaschewski" />

==Recognition==
Nelson is the namesake, along with [[Cecilia Krieger]], of the [[Krieger–Nelson Prize]],  which is awarded to a female mathematician in recognition
of outstanding achievement.<ref name="cmsBio" /> The Department of Mathematics at [[McMaster University]] has a lecture series, "The Evelyn
Nelson Lectures", held since 1991.<ref name="MacLect">[http://www.math.mcmaster.ca/talks/nelson_lectures.php The Evelyn Nelson Lectures] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110706185357/http://www.math.mcmaster.ca/talks/nelson_lectures.php |date=2011-07-06 }}.</ref>
